cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine check the fixed assets for HANGS Construction: equipment and vehicles kept for years.
First, the asset list agrees with the books.
Next, October's new assets. Delivery, setup and tax belong in an asset's cost, but a repair and some low-cost items don't: they're expenses.
A trailer sold for $12,000 was still on the books.
Depreciation spreads cost over the years of use.
It carries last month's totals forward to October. They tie to the books.
Last, it writes the workpapers and an unsigned memo for the controller, the head of accounting.

All done. The assets now cost just over $322,000, and are worth about $232,600 after depreciation. Three journal entries, corrections to the books worth about $63,800 in all, are proposed, including a $7,500 loss on the trailer sale. Five items are open. Nothing is posted until the controller approves.
